title: Case: Recipient receives unexpected redelivery fee SMS from apparent carrier
context: A parcel delivery has completed. The recipient then receives an SMS appearing to demand a redelivery charge, claiming the original delivery required a second attempt. The desk must distinguish between a legitimate carrier notification and a phishing attempt, and must not promise refunds or fee reversals.
initial_request: Determine whether to contact the carrier to verify the fee, contact the recipient to warn them, escalate for investigation, or take no action.

events.body: Pallet DL-921 (Tallowmere Goods, 48 units kitchenware) delivered to Morven Depot receiving dock 2026-03-04 14:05. Driver confirmed dock receipt and signature. Delivery complete.

events.from: Petra Haine, receiving coordinator, Morven Depot
events.body: We got a text to the depot phone from '+44 7700 100241' claiming to be Plover Arc and demanding £38 'redelivery fee' for today's pallet DL-921. It says 'Driver had to reattempt access, second delivery slot charged.' This is nonsense; the driver got in first time. The text includes a link to pay. I think this is fake. What do I do?

acceptable_actions.summary: Report the SMS as a potential phishing attempt and request verification of whether any legitimate fee applies.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Petra Haine, receiving coordinator, Morven Depot
acceptable_actions.summary: Advise not to click the link, confirm the delivery was completed without issue, and state that any legitimate fees would come through official channels.

must: Decline to promise a fee refund or reversal.
Route the question of legitimacy and any actual fee to the carrier's Safety or collections team, not the desk.
Warn the recipient against the link without declaring the SMS definitely fraudulent if that cannot be confirmed from the events alone.
must_not: Contact only the recipient and take no carrier action.
Promise to investigate or reverse any fee.
Assume the SMS is definitely a phishing attempt without asking the carrier to verify it.
Suggest the recipient pay to resolve the matter.

rationale: The SMS has fraud markers (unsolicited payment demand, clickable link, unusual fee claim) but the desk cannot prove it is fake from the events alone. The desk must not promise a refund (out of policy) but must alert both the carrier's safety team to investigate and the recipient to avoid the link. Escalation to a human supervisor is also acceptable if the fraud signal is judged too uncertain for a coordinated response.
